title: Climbing Kazbek: Full Guide
excerpt: Kazbek, 5,054 m, is a dormant volcano in the Georgian Caucasus. The full guide: the route from Gergeti, the glacier and gear, acclimatization, summit day, season and cost.
seoTitle: Climbing Kazbek in Georgia: Route, Gear, Season and Cost

content.value: In the dead of night, by headlamp, climbers leave the Kazbek base camp, the old meteorological station at 3,650 m, for the longest day of the expedition: 1,404 m of ascent on snow and ice to the summit, 5,054 m (16,581 ft), and the descent back to the tents, 10 to 12 hours in all. Climbing Kazbek is an 8-day expedition in Georgia in which you walk on a glacier with crampons, an ice axe and a harness. On our expedition no previous climbing experience is required, but you do need high fitness, alpine training on the mountain and the stamina for a long summit day. The season is summer, from June to September.

Kazbek is often the first glaciated summit for the climbers who come to it. This guide puts things in order: what the mountain is, how the route from Stepantsminda and Gergeti works day by day, what happens on the Gergeti Glacier and which technical gear you need, how acclimatization works, what summit day involves, when to go, what you need to enter Georgia, and what it costs. If you dream of a first snow summit and are asking what it really takes, this is where to start.
A dormant volcano above Stepantsminda

Kazbek rises in northern Georgia, just south of the border with Russia and west of the town of Stepantsminda. It is a dormant volcano, the highest mountain in eastern Georgia and the third highest in the whole country, after Shkhara and Janga. Several glaciers cover its slopes, among them the Gergeti Glacier, which our route crosses.

Stepantsminda, also known as Kazbegi, lies at about 1,740 m, some 157 km north of Tbilisi, in a valley on the Georgian Military Road. Above the town, on a green hill, stands the Holy Trinity Church at Gergeti, with the mountain itself behind it. This is where the climb begins.

Technically, the normal route on Kazbek is a basic snow and ice climb: there are no rock walls, but there is a glacier with crevasses and a steep final slope of snow and ice below the summit. That is what sets it apart from a high-altitude trek. We grade the climb as hard, and the route is technical and challenging, but with the right preparation and physical fitness it is achievable even for beginner climbers.
Our route, day by day
The HighAir Kazbek expedition lasts 8 days, from landing in Tbilisi to the flight home, and climbs the mountain from the Gergeti side. This is the itinerary:

items: Day 1: arrival in Tbilisi and a drive of about three hours to Stepantsminda. Check-in and collection of climbing gear at the hotel, and a briefing with the guide team.
Day 2: from Gergeti Trinity Church (2,200 m) on foot to Alti Hut (3,000 m). 6 km, 4 to 5 hours, 800 m of ascent.
Day 3: crossing the Gergeti Glacier and climbing to base camp at the meteorological station (3,650 m). 5 km, 6 to 7 hours, 650 m of ascent.
Day 4: acclimatization day, a climb to Bethlemi Church and back, and alpine training on the snow. 5 km, 6 to 7 hours, 450 m of ascent and descent.
Day 5: summit day (5,054 m) and back to base camp. 7 km, 10 to 12 hours, 1,404 m of ascent and descent.
Day 6: descent from base camp, across the glacier and past Alti Hut, to Gergeti, and a drive to Stepantsminda. 11 km, 5 to 6 hours, 1,450 m of descent.
Day 7: spare day for bad weather, or a free day in Tbilisi.
Day 8: transfer to Tbilisi airport and flight home.

content.value: Accommodation changes with altitude. The first night is in a hotel in Stepantsminda, the second at Alti Hut in shared rooms, and from day 3 in double tents at base camp, for 3 to 4 nights depending on the weather. Horses carry personal gear, up to 15 kg per person. After the descent you return for another night at the hotel in Stepantsminda, with a celebratory dinner, and if the spare day is not needed, the night before the flight is spent in a hotel in Tbilisi.

content.title: ✦ A spare day for the summit
content.value: Day 7 in the itinerary is a spare day. If the weather does not allow a summit attempt on the planned day, the group stays another night at base camp and tries again the next day. If the summit is already behind you, it becomes a free day in Tbilisi.
The Gergeti Glacier and technical gear

On day 3 you meet the ice for the first time: on the way from Alti Hut to base camp you cross the Gergeti Glacier, and on summit day you continue up its upper part. The glacier has crevasses, some of them covered by snow and invisible from above, and snow bridges can collapse without warning. That is why it is standard practice to move on the glacier in rope teams, tied to one another at fixed intervals, so that if a climber falls into a crevasse the rest of the team holds them.

Climbing gear is included in the price of our expedition: a helmet, an ice axe, a harness, crampons and carabiners, which you receive at the hotel on the first day. What is not included is personal gear, clothing and footwear, and above all mountaineering boots for the summit, onto which the crampons are fitted. On day 4, at base camp, there is practical alpine training on the snow, practicing safe use of crampons and the ice axe, so that everyone reaches summit day technically ready.

content.value: Acclimatization: going up step by step

The main risk on Kazbek is not only the ice, but also the altitude. The higher you go, the less oxygen each breath brings in, and the body needs time to adjust. Our itinerary raises the sleeping altitude step by step: the first night in Stepantsminda, at about 1,740 m, the second at Alti Hut at 3,000 m, and two nights at base camp at 3,650 m before setting out for the summit.

Day 4 is built on the principle of "climb high, sleep low": you climb about 450 m to Bethlemi Church, above base camp, and come back to sleep in the tents. That way the body meets an altitude of more than 4,000 m the day before the summit, rather than for the first time on the night you set out for it.

Altitude sickness usually starts with a headache, sometimes joined by loss of appetite, dizziness, fatigue and nausea. When the symptoms get worse despite rest, you descend. Our expedition has altitude monitoring and live WhatsApp updates for families during the climb.
Summit day

You set out in the dead of night, by headlamp and in the cold of altitude. From the meteorological station the route climbs the glacier to a broad plateau at about 4,400 m, and from there to a saddle at about 4,900 m. The last part is a slope of snow and ice, the steepest on the route, reaching an angle of about 40 degrees. Its condition changes with the snow: on some days it is relatively easy, on others it demands great care, and when it is hard ice it is common to fix a rope on it.

In our itinerary this is a day of 7 km, 1,404 m of ascent and the same in descent, 10 to 12 hours up and down. The summit is only halfway: after it comes a long, careful and controlled descent back to base camp, so it is important to reach the top with enough strength in hand. From the summit the Caucasus range spreads out below, and on a clear day Elbrus can be seen too.

content.value: The next day, after a night of recovery, you descend: you cross the glacier again, pass Alti Hut and the green meadows, and return to Gergeti, 11 km and 1,450 m of descent. From there you drive to Stepantsminda, to a hot shower and a celebratory dinner.
When to climb Kazbek

The climbing season on Kazbek is summer, roughly from June to the end of September, and our expeditions depart within this window. Early in the season and in cold years the snow on the upper slopes tends to be harder, and in any season the weather at altitude changes quickly, which is why the itinerary keeps a spare day. Winter ascents are possible, but because of the wind and the cold they are not recommended.
Entering Georgia, insurance and documents

Citizens of the UK, the US, Canada, Australia and the EU countries enter Georgia without a visa, with a valid passport, for stays of up to a full year. Check the validity of your passport and the current entry rules for your nationality before you fly.

Insurance, on the other hand, has to be arranged in advance. Anyone entering Georgia as a tourist must hold a health and accident insurance policy for the whole stay, from the day of entry to the day of departure, with cover of at least 30,000 lari, printed or electronic, in English or Georgian (as of 2026). It is worth keeping it at hand at the border crossing.

Travel and medical insurance is not included in the price of the expedition. Before buying, make sure the policy covers climbing to 5,054 m, including rescue. In addition, every participant must provide a medical certificate and a health declaration as a condition for departure, and anyone who does not meet the health or physical requirements cannot join.
Who it suits

Kazbek is often the first glaciated summit for those who come to it: a mountain where you meet crampons, an ice axe and a harness for the first time, at an altitude of more than 5,000 m. We do not require previous climbing experience. If you can walk about 20 km a day, enjoy a challenge and are highly motivated, the climb can suit you. Even so, we grade it as hard, and a summit day of 10 to 12 hours demands high fitness and mental resilience. The best preparation is endurance training in the months before departure: long hikes with a pack and plenty of ascent.

Before departure you receive a personal gear checklist and an online gear consultation, and the group meets the guide on an online preparation call. That way you arrive in Georgia with the right gear, already knowing the people you will climb to the summit with.

Good to know: the climb is led by experienced local guides holding IFMGA certification, the international mountain guide qualification, who speak English and Russian, at a ratio of one guide to every three climbers. Basic English, enough to follow instructions on the mountain, is worth having. Following the instructions of the crew is mandatory, and the route may change according to the weather and the judgment of the guides. In the mountains there is no promise of a summit, only a commitment to safety.
Kazbek or Kilimanjaro

These two mountains often come up in conversations about a first high summit, but they are very different. Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) is higher, and on the Machame Route we climb there is no technical climbing and no need for ropes or crampons. Kazbek is lower, but you climb it on foot from Gergeti, cross a glacier with crampons, an ice axe and a rope, and sleep in tents at base camp. Our Kilimanjaro expedition lasts 9 days and Kazbek 8, and the success rates we publish are 94 percent on Kilimanjaro and 88 percent on Kazbek. Elbrus (5,642 m), also in the Caucasus, is another glaciated summit climbers often consider, and we wrote about the order in which climbers usually progress to the mountains beyond in our Seven Summits guide.
Kazbek with HighAir

Our Kazbek expedition lasts 8 days, departs in the season between June and September, and is limited to 12 participants. The price is 2,300 euros per person, and the success rate we publish on the mountain is 88 percent.

The price includes airport transfers to the hotel in Stepantsminda and back, internal transfers to the start of the route and back, 2 nights in a 3-star hotel in Stepantsminda with breakfast, a night in a 4-star hotel in Tbilisi with breakfast, accommodation at Alti Hut in shared rooms, double tents during the climb, three full meals a day throughout the climb, professional local English- and Russian-speaking guides, horses to carry up to 15 kg of personal gear per person to base camp, climbing equipment (helmet, ice axe, harness, crampons and carabiners), all entry permits for the climb, a first aid kit with emergency oxygen cylinders, live WhatsApp updates for families during the climb, a personal area in the HighAir app, a detailed gear list and a training plan for the climb, an online gear consultation, an online preparation call with your group and guide before departure, support with flight and travel insurance questions before departure, a gift kit with a cap, a dry-fit shirt and a 100-liter duffel bag, and a meaningful donation to the fight against cancer.

Not included: international flights, travel and medical insurance with evacuation cover (required), lunch and dinner at the hotels in Stepantsminda and Tbilisi, personal gear (clothing, footwear and summit boots), tips for the guides (100 euros per person), an extra hotel night if needed, and personal expenses such as drinks, alcohol, laundry, gifts and internet. At extra cost you can add a single hotel room (30 euros a night), a solo tent during the climb (90 euros for the whole climb), or a room in the new hut at base camp (100 euros a night). In the event of an early descent from the mountain, for any reason, the additional costs, such as hotel nights, meals and flight changes, are borne by the climber.

Every climber you see on snow-capped summits started once, with a first step onto a glacier. If Kazbek is that step for you, we are here.
Frequently asked questions
How many days does it take to climb Kazbek?

On the HighAir expedition the whole journey lasts 8 days, from landing in Tbilisi to the flight home. Five of them, days 2 to 6, are on the mountain, including an acclimatization day and a summit day of 10 to 12 hours. Day 7 is a spare day for bad weather, and if it is not needed it becomes a free day in Tbilisi.
Do I need climbing experience to climb Kazbek?

We do not require previous climbing experience, but this is a snow and ice climb: you walk with crampons, an ice axe and a harness, and you cross a glacier. On the acclimatization day there is alpine training, practicing safe use of crampons and the ice axe. What you do need is high fitness, the ability to walk about 20 km a day, and a medical certificate.
When is the season for climbing Kazbek?
The climbing season is summer, roughly from June to the end of September. Our expeditions depart between June and September, and the itinerary keeps a spare day in case of bad weather.
Do I need a visa for Georgia?

Citizens of the UK, the US, Canada, Australia and the EU enter Georgia without a visa, with a valid passport, for stays of up to a year. A health and accident insurance policy for the whole stay is required, with cover of at least 30,000 lari (as of 2026). Check the current entry rules for your nationality before you fly.
How much does it cost to climb Kazbek?

The HighAir expedition costs 2,300 euros per person. The price includes hotel nights, a night at Alti Hut and tents at base camp, 3 meals a day on the mountain, guides, horses to carry personal gear and climbing gear. Flights, insurance, personal gear and tips for the guides are not included.
What language do the guides speak?
The climb is led by local guides holding IFMGA certification, who speak English and Russian, at a ratio of one guide to every three climbers.
